title: In a pushout square along a monomorphism the kernels of two parallel sides are isomorphic
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $f:w\to y$, $g:w\to x$, $h:y\to z$, $k:x\to z$ be morphisms of $\mathcal A$ with $h\circ f=k\circ g$ such that the square is cocartesian, i.e. $(z,h,k)$ is a pushout of $f$ and $g$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and assume that $g$ is a monomorphism. Let $\iota_f:\operatorname{Ker}(f)\to w$ and $\iota_k:\operatorname{Ker}(k)\to x$ be kernels. Then the unique morphism $\kappa:\operatorname{Ker}(f)\to\operatorname{Ker}(k)$ with $\iota_k\circ\kappa=g\circ\iota_f$ (it exists since $k\circ g\circ\iota_f=h\circ f\circ\iota_f=0$) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 08N4 (lemma-cartesian-cocartesian, line 887), part (2): a cocartesian square with $g$ mono is cartesian; then Lemma Tag 08N3 (lemma-cartesian-kernel, line 852), part (1): in a cartesian square the map $\operatorname{Ker}(f)\to\operatorname{Ker}(k)$ induced by $g$ is an isomorphism

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: with t=f, l=g, r=h, b=k and sq : IsPushout f g h k, kernel.map f k g h sq.w : kernel f ⟶ kernel k is the morphism kappa (kernel.map ≫ kernel.ι k = kernel.ι f ≫ g) and is an epimorphism by Abelian.epi_kernel_map_of_isPushout (line 151); it is a monomorphism because its composite with kernel.ι k equals kernel.ι f ≫ g, a composite of monomorphisms (mono_of_mono); an abelian category is balanced, so it is an isomorphism (isIso_of_mono_of_epi); any other choice of kernels differs by unique isomorphisms
